module_document.title: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide transport
module_document.description: ATP-driven delivery of lipopolysaccharide or lipooligosaccharide from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane to the bacterial cell surface. Coupled LptBFG extraction, LptC-mediated coupling, periplasmic LptA-family transfer and LptD-mediated outer-membrane insertion form a trans-envelope bridge. The canonical LptDE terminal assembly and the meningococcal LptD-dependent surface-delivery profile differ in their requirement for LptE. Accessory LptM and LptY support terminal transport in characterized enterobacterial systems without defining universal components.

evidence.title: lipopolysaccharide transport
evidence.statement: GO:0015920 grounds movement of LPS from the inner membrane to the cell surface through the trans-envelope Lpt system.

evidence.title: lipopolysaccharide transport system
evidence.statement: GO:0062051 (is_a GO:1990351 transporter complex) is the GO complex term for the whole trans-envelope Lpt machine; its definition cites PMID:29449493.

evidence.title: Regulated assembly of the transenvelope protein complex required for lipopolysaccharide export.
evidence.statement: Defines the seven essential Lpt proteins and the transenvelope bridge model on which the module's three parts are based.
evidence.supporting_text: In Escherichia coli, this LPS transport process is known to require the seven essential Lpt proteins,7 but how these proteins move large, amphipathic LPS molecules across both membranes and the periplasmic space is not understood.

evidence.title: Functional analysis of the protein machinery required for transport of lipopolysaccharide to the outer membrane of Escherichia coli.
evidence.statement: Places LptA, LptB, LptC, LptD and LptE in one LPS transport machine.
evidence.supporting_text: In this paper we provide evidence that LptA, LptB, LptD, LptE, and YrbK (renamed LptC), an essential IM protein characterized here, are all members of the same LPS transport machinery.

evidence.title: Identification of two inner-membrane proteins required for the transport of lipopolysaccharide to the outer membrane of Escherichia coli.
evidence.statement: Identifies LptF and LptG as the transmembrane subunits of the LptB-energized extraction transporter.
evidence.supporting_text: We propose that these two proteins, which we have renamed LptF and LptG, respectively, are the missing transmembrane components of the ABC transporter that, together with LptB, functions to extract LPS from the IM en route to the OM.

evidence.title: Pseudomonas putida KT2440 lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis
evidence.statement: KEGG ppu00540 includes the P. putida KT2440 Lpt components associated with LPS biogenesis and export, supporting the KT2440 exemplars.

evidence.title: Transport of lipopolysaccharide to the Gram-negative bacterial cell surface.
evidence.statement: Lpt-related homologs occur in multiple non-proteobacterial diderms and in diderms lacking LPS; a homolog is not sufficient evidence of LPS substrate transport. Review includes sequence/domain survey; n.d. means not detected, not proved absent. LPS biosynthesis, MsbA flipping and O-antigen assembly are upstream of the selected outer-IM-leaflet to OM-surface transport mechanism. The review distinguishes synthesis/flipping from Lpt-mediated export. The review recognizes the Neisseria LptE exception and directs readers to the primary surface-accessibility study. E. coli seven-component essentiality is not a universal taxon rule.

evidence.title: Structural Insights into the Lipopolysaccharide Transport (Lpt) System as a Novel Antibiotic Target.
evidence.statement: The inner-membrane ABC assembly extracts mature outer-leaflet LPS and couples cytoplasmic nucleotide turnover to transport. LptC links the extractor to the bridge and modulates ATPase behavior. Complex activity; not autonomous transport by an isolated ATPase or permease. Aligned hydrophobic grooves in LptF/C/A/D support transport across the aqueous periplasm. The review provides an architecture overview, not target-specific quantitative kinetics. LptD and LptE organize the terminal translocon and selective outer-leaflet insertion. General canonical model, qualified by lineage-specific primary evidence and later LptM/Y work.

evidence.title: Lipid Transport Across Bacterial Membranes.
evidence.statement: Lpt differs from MsbA: extraction starts in the outer IM leaflet, followed by periplasmic movement and selective OM insertion. No IM transbilayer activity is assigned to LptBFG. The number of native LptA molecules and accommodation of different periplasmic widths remained open questions. Do not assert a universal fixed oligomer count from in vitro polymerization. Hydrophobic grooves connect the inner membrane extractor to LptDE; the OM headgroup route and lateral lipid-anchor exit are distinct aspects of delivery. Structural/mechanistic review, not independent experimental validation of each taxon.

evidence.title: The LptD chaperone LptE is not directly involved in lipopolysaccharide transport in Neisseria meningitidis.
evidence.statement: LptE deletion preserves surface-accessible LPS in the tested meningococcal backgrounds while reducing LptD abundance, supporting a chaperone/biogenesis role. LptE dispensability for that endpoint differs from absence of all possible contributions. LptH/C/F/G mutants fail cell-surface accessibility assays. LptC/B/H conditional depletion reduces cellular LPS, restored by expression. Viability without LPS is not normal LPS transport; no native LptC-independent pathway is established. Meningococcal carrier LptH is distinct from the lipid A phosphoethanolamine transferase also called LptA. Q7DDQ9 is the carrier, even though its UniProt gene field uses lptA.

evidence.title: The Lack of the Essential LptC Protein in the Trans-Envelope Lipopolysaccharide Transport Machine Is Circumvented by Suppressor Mutations in LptF, an Inner Membrane Component of the Escherichia coli Transporter.
evidence.statement: Conditional compensation establishes that missing LptC is not biologically impossible in all genetic backgrounds. Keep the canonical supported profile separate from experimentally selected bypass; do not invent a normal ancestral route from the authors hypothesis. The 2016 paper also summarizes prior E. coli complementation by Pa LptC under elevated LptB expression; a blanket assertion of impossible heterologous substitution is too strong. Prior-study context, not newly assayed in PMID41407669; normal compatibility still requires positive matched-interface support.

evidence.title: Structural basis of lipopolysaccharide assembly by the outer membrane translocon holo-complex.
evidence.statement: LptM occupies the lateral-gate region and influences LPS access; LptY stabilizes the periplasmic LptD receptor domain. Positive roles exceed a generic assembly-only description, while the detailed contraction/extension cycle remains partly mechanistic proposal. Together the accessory lipoproteins improve connection of the translocon to the inner-membrane transport machinery. Supported optional lineage-qualified efficiency/organization roles, not compulsory components in every LPS-producing organism. LptM also contributes to LptD oxidative maturation, whereas LptY did not show the same maturation role. Distinguish biogenesis from transport contribution; neither is added as a separate chemical reaction.

evidence.title: Structural basis for regulating lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transport.
evidence.statement: Bridge assembly and LPS occupancy regulate TM-LptC displacement and ATP binding/hydrolysis, linking completion of the bridge to productive activity. Biochemical and E. coli cellular support; engineered structural stabilization is explicit. LptC is both a structural coupling element and part of regulatory gating of extraction. Do not convert substrate-driven mechanical regulation into an unsupported separate signal-transduction function. A viable engineered LptC–LptA fusion supports the bridge mechanism but does not establish native universal LptA stoichiometry. Native architecture and engineered construct are distinguished.

evidence.title: Structural snapshots of Pseudomonas aeruginosa LptB(2)FG and LptB(2)FGC reveal insights into lipopolysaccharide recognition and transport.
evidence.statement: Cryo-EM and native MS characterize Pa LptBFG and LptBFGC states, LPS recognition and lipid interactions. Structural/substrate-binding evidence and ATPase competence do not alone reconstruct complete trans-envelope transport. Binding preferences for Pa versus E. coli LPS support substrate sensitivity, and cardiolipin binding/competition complicates a simplistic LPS-only binding claim. Heterogeneous commercial LPS and purified assemblies; no new phospholipid-transport function or native KT2440 kinetics inferred.

evidence.title: Identification of an outer membrane protein required for the transport of lipopolysaccharide to the bacterial cell surface.
evidence.statement: Loss of Imp/LptD prevents proper surface exposure of residual LPS, assessed through extracellular accessibility and an OM modification assay. Strain H44/76 direct evidence; no purified isolated-protein insertion kinetics claimed.

module_document.notes: Boundary: mature LPS/LOS in the outer IM leaflet to exposure in the outer OM leaflet; synthesis, MsbA flipping and O-antigen elaboration are upstream. Bacteria is the shared taxon envelope, not a universal capacity assertion. LPS substrate, a diderm envelope and a compatible extraction/bridge/insertion system are necessary scope conditions. Lpt-like sequences in LPS-free diderms do not establish this substrate-specific process. E. coli and P. putida provide complete seven-component reviewed panels; the three Neisseria representatives establish a distinct terminal-role boundary and carrier evidence, not a complete reviewed extractor panel. Native Neisseria assays are H44/76 or HB-1; MC58 LptE/LptH are exact protein-sequence matches, not native MC58 phenotype assays. Meningococcal viability after LPS loss does not establish transport: LptC/H/F/G mutants fail surface accessibility, whereas LptE deletion preserves detectable surface LPS. Selected E. coli LptF suppressors bypass LptC; canonical missing-C failures do not imply impossibility in every genetic background. Cross-species interfaces require positive support: Pa LptC complementation can depend on elevated LptB expression. The 2026 E. coli fusion bridge expressed in an LPS-null Acinetobacter host is neither a native Acinetobacter panel nor proof of universal one-copy LptA stoichiometry. Permease ATP-coupling, carrier transfer, terminal insertion and accessory stabilization are distinct roles; no autonomous transport is assigned to isolated accessory proteins. Original and new gene-review consultations, searched review articles, source identity and conditional scope are documented under analysis/module_audits/bacterial_lps_transport. The actual module Falcon request failed HTTP403; manual literature assessment is recorded separately. Capacity evaluation additionally requires the documented positive subunit roles, substrate, ATP supply, lineage and matched-interface gates; bare family/GO matches or Boolean satisfiability alone do not establish a functional Lpt system. The capacity audit records these external evidence requirements and compiler limitations.

findings.statement: The inner-membrane ABC assembly extracts mature outer-leaflet LPS and couples cytoplasmic nucleotide turnover to transport. LptC links the extractor to the bridge and modulates ATPase behavior. Complex activity; not autonomous transport by an isolated ATPase or permease.
Aligned hydrophobic grooves in LptF/C/A/D support transport across the aqueous periplasm. The review provides an architecture overview, not target-specific quantitative kinetics.
LptD and LptE organize the terminal translocon and selective outer-leaflet insertion. General canonical model, qualified by lineage-specific primary evidence and later LptM/Y work.

findings.statement: Lpt differs from MsbA: extraction starts in the outer IM leaflet, followed by periplasmic movement and selective OM insertion. No IM transbilayer activity is assigned to LptBFG.
The number of native LptA molecules and accommodation of different periplasmic widths remained open questions. Do not assert a universal fixed oligomer count from in vitro polymerization.

Hydrophobic grooves connect the inner membrane extractor to LptDE; the OM headgroup route and lateral lipid-anchor exit are distinct aspects of delivery. Structural/mechanistic review, not independent experimental validation of each taxon.

findings.statement: Cryo-EM and native MS characterize Pa LptBFG and LptBFGC states, LPS recognition and lipid interactions. Structural/substrate-binding evidence and ATPase competence do not alone reconstruct complete trans-envelope transport.

Binding preferences for Pa versus E. coli LPS support substrate sensitivity, and cardiolipin binding/competition complicates a simplistic LPS-only binding claim. Heterogeneous commercial LPS and purified assemblies; no new phospholipid-transport function or native KT2440 kinetics inferred.

findings.statement: LptM occupies the lateral-gate region and influences LPS access; LptY stabilizes the periplasmic LptD receptor domain. Positive roles exceed a generic assembly-only description, while the detailed contraction/extension cycle remains partly mechanistic proposal.

Together the accessory lipoproteins improve connection of the translocon to the inner-membrane transport machinery. Supported optional lineage-qualified efficiency/organization roles, not compulsory components in every LPS-producing organism.

LptM also contributes to LptD oxidative maturation, whereas LptY did not show the same maturation role. Distinguish biogenesis from transport contribution; neither is added as a separate chemical reaction.

findings.statement: Bridge assembly and LPS occupancy regulate TM-LptC displacement and ATP binding/hydrolysis, linking completion of the bridge to productive activity. Biochemical and E. coli cellular support; engineered structural stabilization is explicit.

LptC is both a structural coupling element and part of regulatory gating of extraction. Do not convert substrate-driven mechanical regulation into an unsupported separate signal-transduction function.
A viable engineered LptC–LptA fusion supports the bridge mechanism but does not establish native universal LptA stoichiometry. Native architecture and engineered construct are distinguished.

findings.statement: LptE deletion preserves surface-accessible LPS in the tested meningococcal backgrounds while reducing LptD abundance, supporting a chaperone/biogenesis role. LptE dispensability for that endpoint differs from absence of all possible contributions.

LptH/C/F/G mutants fail cell-surface accessibility assays. LptC/B/H conditional depletion reduces cellular LPS, restored by expression. Viability without LPS is not normal LPS transport; no native LptC-independent pathway is established.
Meningococcal carrier LptH is distinct from the lipid A phosphoethanolamine transferase also called LptA. Q7DDQ9 is the carrier, even though its UniProt gene field uses lptA.

findings.statement: Conditional compensation establishes that missing LptC is not biologically impossible in all genetic backgrounds. Keep the canonical supported profile separate from experimentally selected bypass; do not invent a normal ancestral route from the authors hypothesis.

The 2016 paper also summarizes prior E. coli complementation by Pa LptC under elevated LptB expression; a blanket assertion of impossible heterologous substitution is too strong. Prior-study context, not newly assayed in PMID41407669; normal compatibility still requires positive matched-interface support.
